newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-STUTTGART AND DORTMUND BOTH HIT FIVE IN BUNDESLIGA ROMPS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-STUTTGART AND DORTMUND BOTH HIT FIVE IN BUNDESLIGA ROMPS.

text.p: German first division leaders VfB Stuttgart and reigning champions Borussia Dortmund both underlined their challenge for the title on Saturday with five-goal romps against lowly opposition.
International striker Fredi Bobic hit a hat-trick for 1992 champions Stuttgart as they trounced troubled Borussia Moenchengladbach 5-0, taking his personal tally to 10 goals from 12 games.

Brazilian defender Julio Cesar, labouring with a knee injury, struck the first two goals for Dortmund in a 5-0 win over bottom club Arminia Bielefeld to give them the perfect boost before Wednesday's Champions' League match against Atletico Madrid.

Thirteen-times champions Bayern Munich kept up with the pace at the top by winning 2-0 at Fortuna Duesseldorf to jump over Bayer Leverkusen into second place on 27 points, behind Stuttgart on goal difference.

Stuttgart's win was a triumph for their "magic triangle" of Bobic, Giovane Elber and Krasimir Balakov against an inept Moenchengladbach side missing injured skipper and midfield inspiration Stefan Effenberg.
Bobic, now the league's leading scorer, pounced as early as the third minute, and playmaker Balakov set up the second for the Brazilian Elber in the 56th.
Moenchengladbach failed to take comfort from the news that Swedish forward Martin Dahlin is returning after just four months with AS Roma, and crumbled under the onslaught.
"At 2-0 down, the dam just burst," said coach Bernd Krauss, whose dispirited side must travel to Monaco in the UEFA Cup this week hoping to overturn a 4-2 first leg deficit.
Balakov converted a penalty in the 68th minute, and Bobic completed his hat-trick with two goals in the last 13 minutes.

Cesar gave Dortmund the lead against Bielefeld with a 10th minute header but Bielefeld gave as good as they got until 42-year-old 'keeper Uli Stein failed to punch out a corner just before half-time, leaving Cesar to side-foot into an open goal.

Heiko Herrlich added to Stein's misery by slotting the ball through his legs in the 54th minute, and in-form Rene Tretschok and Stephane Chapuisat bagged a goal each from close range in the 77th and 82nd minutes.
The win was doubly satisfying for Dortmund trainer Ottmar Hitzfeld, whose squad has been badly hit by injury all season and who has had to fend off reports of bickering in the team.
"After the first half we should have been trailing but in the second half we were like a well-oiled machine," he said.
Dortmund's win took them into fourth place on 23 points, one behind Leverkusen, who drew 1-1 at Werder Bremen on Friday.
Bayern did an efficient but lacklustre job at Duesseldorf against one of the most dogged defences in the league.
Dieter Hamann scored in the 38th minute after a one-two with Juergen Klinsmann, and Mehmet Scholl sealed matters with a solo run seven minutes from time.
